title: PTNK 2022 · Tiếng Anh Không chuyên
subtitle: Đề thi tuyển sinh lớp 10 · Trường Phổ thông Năng khiếu · 2022-2023
source: 2022 Thi vào 10 Đề thi Anh chung Phổ thông Năng khiếu.pdf

questions.q: Choose the word whose underlined part is pronounced differently from those of the other words.
questions.explanation: In honest the "h" is silent (/ˈɒnɪst/); in human, hidden and helpful it is pronounced /h/.

questions.q: Choose the word whose underlined part is pronounced differently from those of the other words.
questions.explanation: insist has the short /ɪ/ sound; decide, define and night all have the diphthong /aɪ/.

questions.q: Choose the word whose underlined part is pronounced differently from those of the other words.
questions.explanation: After a voiced sound (/n/) the ending is pronounced /d/ in declined; after the voiceless /k/, /f/ and /p/ it is /t/ in looked, laughed and hoped.

questions.q: Choose the word whose primary stress is placed on a syllable different from those in the other words.
questions.explanation: GAther is stressed on the first syllable; preFER, surPRISE and deFINE are stressed on the second.

questions.q: Choose the word whose primary stress is placed on a syllable different from those in the other words.
questions.explanation: DIfficult is stressed on the first syllable; diSASter, deLIGHTful and disTRACtion are stressed on the second.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: When our family was on holiday, our neighbor helped us by ______ our garden plants.
questions.explanation: look after = take care of. "Taking care" would need "of", and "look up"/"care about" do not fit plants.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: As an only child, Mary wishes that she ______ at least one sibling to play with every day.
questions.explanation: A wish about the present takes the past simple: wish + (that) + S + V-ed → "wishes that she had".

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: In their lesson yesterday, Linda's tutor ______ follow the model essay rigidly to gain a good score.
questions.explanation: Pattern advise + object + not + to-infinitive; "yesterday" requires the past tense "advised".

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: Nancy is a hard-working and smart student. Rarely ______ any homework exercise unfinished.
questions.explanation: A negative adverb like Rarely at the start of a sentence forces inversion: Rarely + auxiliary + subject + verb.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: If the Smiths follow a clean-eating meal plan, they ______ cut down on fat and sugar.
questions.explanation: Only must can take the bare infinitive "cut" directly; "have" and "ought" need "to", and "had better" is followed by a bare infinitive, not "to".

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: It's too cold out there in the park! Put on your ______ to keep warm.
questions.explanation: Cold weather calls for a wool sweater; a skirt, shorts or a short-sleeved blouse would not keep anyone warm.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: In our training session last week, we met our new football coach ______ here from a city club.
questions.explanation: A reduced relative clause with a perfect participle: "coach having moved here" = who had moved here (before we met him).

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: John's grandfather is interested in history. He likes watching ______ every night.
questions.explanation: Someone interested in history watches documentaries; the other options are not history programmes one "watches every night".

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: Of the three movies I have watched, 3 Idiots is ______.
questions.explanation: "Of the three movies" compares three items, so the superlative the most interesting is needed.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: IELTS is a/an ______ English test whose result is widely accepted in many countries.
questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun "test", and "accepted in many countries" points to international.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: On their Independence Day, American people love watching ______ marching along the streets.
questions.explanation: Only parades can be "marching along the streets".

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: City born and city bred, Jack has never seen how ______ are raised on the farm.
questions.explanation: Animals are raised on a farm; crops and plants are grown, and villages are not raised at all.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: My city gradually returned to normal ______ all lockdown restrictions were removed.
questions.explanation: The city returned to normal gradually, i.e. over time after the restrictions were removed; "as soon as" would contradict "gradually".

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: Lan really loves the song lyrics ______ her father wrote especially for her.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun refers to "the song lyrics" (a thing) and is the object of "wrote", so which is used.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: Our class will join a ______ campaign this summer. This is our school's community program.
questions.explanation: A school community programme would run a beach clean-up campaign; "littering campaign" would mean the opposite.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: A/an ______, or a huge tidal wave, can wash away a whole seaside village.
questions.explanation: The definition "a huge tidal wave" is that of a tsunami.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: Tom's mother gave him a ______ as a birthday gift.
questions.explanation: Adjective order: opinion/age (new) → colour (red) → origin/brand (Nike) → noun: new red Nike cap.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: Replace the leaking faucets or we'll have an enormous ______ as we did last month.
questions.explanation: Leaking faucets waste water, so the result is an enormous water bill.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: On her first vacation to Korea, Ellen was very excited about the diverse ______ of this Asian country.
questions.explanation: "Diverse" describes the variety of a country's culture; "region" and "temple" would need a plural, and "uniqueness" cannot be diverse.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 1: Structure and meaning identification
questions.q: No one believed in Nick's story about his UFO ____ last night during his drive home.
questions.explanation: UFO sighting is the fixed collocation for seeing a UFO.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 2: Error identification
questions.q:
Find ONE error (A, B, C, or D) in the following sentence.
(A) Rainy weather normally (B) effects people's mood, so (C) they tend to avoid the (D) wet season if possible.
questions.explanation: The verb meaning "to influence" is affect; "effect" is a noun. effects → affects.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 2: Error identification
questions.q:
Find ONE error (A, B, C, or D) in the following sentence.
Jack will have (A) to take the online exam again because (B) he (C) did not have Internet (D) assess last week.
questions.explanation: "Internet access" (noun, the ability to connect) is meant; "assess" is a verb meaning to evaluate. assess → access.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 2: Error identification
questions.q:
Find ONE error (A, B, C, or D) in the following sentence.
I (A) can never forget (B) my grandmother's old house (C) was located in a (D) beautifully designed neighborhood.
questions.explanation: The object of "forget" is "my grandmother's old house"; the following clause needs a relative pronoun or a participle: was located → located / which was located.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 2: Error identification
questions.q:
Find ONE error (A, B, C, or D) in the following sentence.
A famous singer (A) had posted a message (B) which hurt her fans, (C) therefore, she had to post (D) an apology.
questions.explanation: "therefore" is an adverb and cannot join two clauses with only a comma; a conjunction is needed: therefore, → so.

questions.part: Section 2: Grammar and Vocabulary · Part 2: Error identification
questions.q:
Find ONE error (A, B, C, or D) in the following sentence.
Being (A) extreme excited (B) as soon as the football match (C) began, little Tom shouted and (D) jumped around.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the adjective "excited": extreme → extremely.

questions.passage:
LIFE DURING THE PANDEMIC
By: Lynda Feustel (adapted)

1. Entering year two of (31)____ pandemic is strange. It barely seems a day since last March 2020, but it also seems like a lifetime. As an only child and introvert, shutting down my world was initially simple and relatively easy. My friends and I had been super busy with the school play, and while I was sad about it being canceled, I was struggling a lot during that show and desperately needed some time (32)____.

2. As March turned to April, virtual school began, and being alone really set in. I missed my friends and us being together. The isolation felt real with just my parents and me, even as we spent time together. My friends and I began meeting on Facetime every night (33)____ TV and just be together in some way. We laughed at insane jokes we made, had homework and therapy sessions over Facetime, and grew closer through digital and literal walls. The summer passed with in-person events together, and the virus faded into the background for a little while. We went to the beach and (34)____ out in people's backyards.

3. Then school came for us in a way none of us had ever expected. In hybrid school we were separated. Students had lessons, sports, and other activities while many of us were in quarantine. Teachers piled on work, and the virus grew more present again. Group texting put out hundreds of messages a day and again, meeting in person as a group (35)____. Being together on video and in person was the way of staying cheered up.

4. We are working and looking for some change as we are about to enter the second year of this pandemic. After all, life is hopeful.
questions.q: Choose the best option for gap (31).
questions.explanation: The pandemic is a specific one already known to the reader, so the definite article the is used.

questions.passage:
By: Lieutenant Brian Ellis (adapted)

1. One of the promises I have made to myself as a leader in recent years is to be more mindful of improving my surroundings every day. This happens mostly through the lessons of life, and pushing into areas that challenge my way of thinking or creating useful opportunities for me to strengthen my values. Any good gift is worth sharing, so I extend the list of books with some following sweet faces of love.

2. Love is patient: The opposite is impatience, a cause of hostility and frustration. According to Challenging the Law Enforcement Organization by Jack Enter, leaders have to make sure they are patient enough for others to go through the processes of learning from mistakes.

3. Love is kind: No employee will follow a controlling leader. Good leaders make people-centered policies because of the benefits and force these policies create. In A Higher Standard of Leadership by Keshavan Nair, it is suggested to look below the surface and identify the hidden needs of others to create a bond with those you are trying to serve.

4. Love does not envy: Envy can be subtle and indirect, and interferes with colleagues, family, and friends, according to Envy and Leadership by Mark Stein. Being truthful to yourself means understanding who you are and who you want to be. Being comfortable with the journey is part of the experience. Having more doesn't fix anything, and the idea of being content is the way to a satisfied heart.

5. Love keeps no record of wrongs: I'm no saint and neither are you. Be compassionate enough for problem solving, which also means you understand when it's time to turn around and reassess. Create an environment that is focused on problem solving rather than people blaming through learning and development.

6. Love always trusts: Trust is challenging at times, and it requires us to confront the things that stand in its way. When we have to protect ourselves from each other, the whole organization suffers. When trust thrives, the organization grows stronger as a result, as illustrated in Leaders Eat Last: Why Some Teams Pull Together and Others Don't by Simon Sinek.

7. All in all, love never fails. It will be the one constant that gives you an inspired life.
questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
questions.explanation: The author, a leader, shares "sweet faces of love" (patient, kind, does not envy…) as lessons drawn from leadership books — lessons of love for leaders.

questions.passage:
1. SARS, Ebola, and SARS-CoV-2: all three of these highly infectious viruses have caused global panic since 2002, and all three of them jumped to humans from wild animals living in dense tropical forests that we are slashing and burning to create land for crops, mining, and housing. The more we clear, the more we come into contact with wildlife which hosts illnesses likely transferred to humans.

2. Stopping deforestation will not only reduce natural disasters but also control the spread of a long list of dangerous diseases that have come from rain forest habitats - Zika, Nipah, malaria, cholera, HIV, and so on. A 2019 study found that a 10 percent increase in deforestation would raise malaria cases by 3.3 percent; that would be 7.4 million people worldwide. Meanwhile, an average of 28 million hectares of forest have been cut down annually since 2016, and there is no sign of a slowdown. [A]

3. Societies can take numerous steps to prevent the destruction. Eating less meat, which improves our health anyway, will lessen demand for crops and pastures. Eating fewer processed foods will reduce the demand for palm oil, much of which is grown on land from tropical rain forests. Producing more food per hectare can boost supply without the need for more land. [B]

4. In the meantime, governments should prohibit the sale of live wild animals in so-called wet markets, where pathogens have repeatedly crossed over into humans. The markets may be culturally important, but the risk is too great. Governments must also ban illegal wildlife trade, which can spread infectious agents far and wide. In addition, authorities must examine factory farms that pack thousands of animals together – the source of the 2009 swine flu outbreak that killed more than 10,000 people in the U.S. and many more people worldwide. [C]

5. Ending deforestation and preventing pandemics would address six of the United Nations' 17 Sustainable Development Goals: the guarantee of healthy lives, zero hunger, gender equality, responsible consumption and production, sustainably managed land, and climate action. The COVID-19 pandemic is a catastrophe, but it calls for our attention on the human achievements by not overexploiting the natural world. [D]

(Adapted from Scientific American)
questions.q: What may be the best title for the passage?
options: How to Stop Deforestation in Worldwide Societies
Deforestation as a Major Cause of Pandemics
questions.explanation: The whole passage links clearing forests to viruses jumping from wild animals to humans and argues that ending deforestation prevents pandemics — deforestation as a cause of pandemics.

The COVID-19 pandemic is a catastrophe, but it calls for our attention on the human achievements by not overexploiting the natural world. [D]

(Adapted from Scientific American)
questions.q: According to paragraph 3, _____ is one step to prevent the destruction.
questions.explanation: "Producing more food per hectare can boost supply without the need for more land" = increased productivity. Eating less meat is not a ban, and reforestation is not mentioned.

questions.passage:
1. SARS, Ebola, and SARS-CoV-2: all three of these highly infectious viruses have caused global panic since 2002, and all three of them jumped to humans from wild animals living in dense tropical forests that we are slashing and burning to create land for crops, mining, and housing. The more we clear, the more we come into contact with wildlife which hosts illnesses likely transferred to humans.

2. Stopping deforestation will not only reduce natural disasters but also control the spread of a long list of dangerous diseases that have come from rain forest habitats - Zika, Nipah, malaria, cholera, HIV, and so on. A 2019 study found that a 10 percent increase in deforestation would raise malaria cases by 3.3 percent; that would be 7.4 million people worldwide. Meanwhile, an average of 28 million hectares of forest have been cut down annually since 2016, and there is no sign of a slowdown. [A]

3. Societies can take numerous steps to prevent the destruction. Eating less meat, which improves our health anyway, will lessen demand for crops and pastures. Eating fewer processed foods will reduce the demand for palm oil, much of which is grown on land from tropical rain forests. Producing more food per hectare can boost supply without the need for more land. [B]

4. In the meantime, governments should prohibit the sale of live wild animals in so-called wet markets, where pathogens have repeatedly crossed over into humans. The markets may be culturally important, but the risk is too great. Governments must also ban illegal wildlife trade, which can spread infectious agents far and wide. In addition, authorities must examine factory farms that pack thousands of animals together – the source of the 2009 swine flu outbreak that killed more than 10,000 people in the U.S. and many more people worldwide. [C]

5. Ending deforestation and preventing pandemics would address six of the United Nations' 17 Sustainable Development Goals: the guarantee of healthy lives, zero hunger, gender equality, responsible consumption and production, sustainably managed land, and climate action. The COVID-19 pandemic is a catastrophe, but it calls for our attention on the human achievements by not overexploiting the natural world. [D]

(Adapted from Scientific American)
questions.q: What is implied in paragraph 4 about sales of live wild animals in wet markets?
options: They must be removed out of all wet markets.
They are illegal and have been long banned.
They are important as they make local culture.
questions.explanation: "The markets may be culturally important, but the risk is too great" — the disadvantages outweigh the advantages.

questions.q:
In which place can the following sentence best fit?
Reducing food waste can also vastly lessen the pressure to grow more crops.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 lists what societies can do to reduce demand for land; "also" adds one more such step, so the sentence fits at [B].

questions.q: Vietnam was ___ successful in its early fight against the Covid-19 virus. (IMPRESS)
accept: impressively
questions.answer: impressively
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the adjective "successful": impressively.

questions.q: Most ___ parks are built in the suburbs, not in city centers. (INDUSTRY)
accept: industrial
questions.answer: industrial
questions.explanation: An adjective before the noun "parks": industrial parks (khu công nghiệp).

questions.q: At colleges and universities, teachers are normally called "___". (INSTRUCT)
accept: instructors
questions.answer: instructors
questions.explanation: A plural noun for people: teachers = instructors.

questions.q: Mary's clothes are always in style because she wants to look ___. (FASHION)
accept: fashionable
questions.answer: fashionable
questions.explanation: After "look" (linking verb) an adjective is needed: fashionable.

questions.q: Young people should work hard to develop their country's ___. (ECONOMICAL)
accept: economy
questions.answer: economy
questions.explanation: After the possessive "country's" a noun is needed: the country's economy.

questions.q: In a written ___, it takes more time for test papers to be marked. (EXAMINE)
accept: examination
exam
questions.answer: examination
questions.explanation: After "a written" a noun is needed: a written examination.

questions.q: The 31st SEA Games event was both ___ and motivational to many people. (ENJOY)
accept: enjoyable
questions.answer: enjoyable
questions.explanation: "both ___ and motivational" needs an adjective parallel to "motivational": enjoyable.

questions.q: It is interesting that many useful products have been ___ by chance. (INVENTION)
accept: invented
questions.answer: invented
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive "have been + past participle": invented.

questions.q: ___ speaking, teenagers are passionate fans of entertainment trends. (GENERAL)
accept: Generally
generally
questions.answer: Generally
questions.explanation: The fixed adverbial phrase Generally speaking = in general.

questions.q: ___ to fluorescent bulbs, LED lights are up to 80% more energy-saving. (COMPARE)
accept: Compared
compared
questions.answer: Compared
questions.explanation: The fixed participle phrase Compared to/with = in comparison with.

questions.q:
It is possible that the Covid-19 is less threatening in many countries now.
→ The Covid-19 virus ___
accept: is likely to be less threatening in many countries now
may be less threatening in many countries now
might be less threatening in many countries now
could be less threatening in many countries now
is possibly less threatening in many countries now
questions.answer: is likely to be less threatening in many countries now
questions.explanation: "It is possible that S + V" → "S is likely to V" or "S may/might V".

questions.q:
They believe that hard work leads to success.
→ It ___
accept: is believed that hard work leads to success
questions.answer: is believed that hard work leads to success
questions.explanation: Impersonal passive with a reporting verb: "They believe that…" → "It is believed that…".

questions.q:
"Don't go to bed late or you'll be late for school tomorrow," Tim's mother said to him.
→ Tim's mother told ___ the next day.
accept: him not to go to bed late or he would be late for school
him not to go to bed late or he'd be late for school
questions.answer: him not to go to bed late or he would be late for school
questions.explanation: Reported command: "told + object + not to + V"; "you'll" becomes "he would" and "tomorrow" becomes "the next day".

questions.q:
I'm dreaming about a vacation by the beach in this hot weather.
→ I wish ___
accept: I were having a vacation by the beach in this hot weather
I was having a vacation by the beach in this hot weather
I could have a vacation by the beach in this hot weather
I had a vacation by the beach in this hot weather
questions.answer: I were having a vacation by the beach in this hot weather
questions.explanation: A wish about the present takes the past (subjunctive "were"): "I wish I were having a vacation…".

questions.q:
Karen's best friend is studying abroad now. He can't attend Karen's 15th birthday.
→ If Karen's best friend ___
accept: were not studying abroad now, he could attend Karen's 15th birthday
weren't studying abroad now, he could attend Karen's 15th birthday
were not studying abroad now, he would be able to attend Karen's 15th birthday
were not studying abroad, he could attend Karen's 15th birthday
was not studying abroad now, he could attend Karen's 15th birthday
wasn't studying abroad now, he could attend Karen's 15th birthday
questions.answer: were not studying abroad now, he could attend Karen's 15th birthday
questions.explanation: Second conditional for an unreal present: "If S were not V-ing, S could V" — the facts are reversed in the if-clause and the result clause.

questions.q:
My cousin rides his bike to work every day, but he thinks going by bus is safer.
→ Riding ___
accept: his bike to work every day, my cousin thinks going by bus is safer
his bike to work daily, my cousin thinks going by bus is safer
questions.answer: his bike to work every day, my cousin thinks going by bus is safer
questions.explanation: A participle clause with the same subject: "Riding his bike to work every day, my cousin thinks…"; the subject "my cousin" must follow the comma.

questions.q:
Learning English through Walt Disney movies is easy for many children.
→ Many children find ___
accept: learning English through Walt Disney movies easy
it easy to learn English through Walt Disney movies
it easy learning English through Walt Disney movies
questions.answer: learning English through Walt Disney movies easy
questions.explanation: Pattern "find + object + adjective": find learning English … easy, or "find it easy to learn…".

questions.q:
If I am admitted into my dream high school, I will try my best for my academic goals.
→ Should ___, I will try my best for my academic goals.
accept: I be admitted into my dream high school
I be admitted to my dream high school
questions.answer: I be admitted into my dream high school
questions.explanation: Inverted first conditional: "If I am admitted" → "Should I be admitted" (should + subject + bare infinitive).

questions.q:
Larry joins some study groups on Facebook, so this social media platform is useful to him.
→ Facebook ___
accept: on which Larry joins some study groups, is useful to him
is useful to Larry because he joins some study groups on it
is a useful platform to Larry because he joins some study groups on it
where Larry joins some study groups, is useful to him
is useful to Larry as he joins some study groups on it
is a useful social media platform to Larry because he joins some study groups on it
questions.answer: on which Larry joins some study groups, is useful to him
questions.explanation: Either a relative clause "Facebook, on which Larry joins some study groups, is useful to him" or a reason clause "Facebook is useful to Larry because he joins some study groups on it".

questions.q:
The new supervisor just made a request. He asked us not to gossip during our meetings.
→ The new supervisor requested that ___
accept: we should not gossip during our meetings
we not gossip during our meetings
we shouldn't gossip during our meetings
questions.answer: we should not gossip during our meetings
questions.explanation: After "request that" the subjunctive is used: "requested that we (should) not gossip…".
